the optical forces exerted on a dielectric waveguide in the presence of a metallic substrate are significantly enhanced compared to the case where the waveguide is suspended in vacuum.
the optical force is enhanced in the hybrid plasmonic mode, compared to the dielectric mode.

the optical force on a suspended dieletric waveguide coupled to an optically dense metallic substrate can be greatly enhanced compared to the force on the same waveguide coupled to optically transparent dielectric substrate, and that the optical force can be tuned to a large extent by changing the waveguide height.

the study of the interaction of light with nanostructures and the development of nanoscale photonic devices based on this interaction.
the development of novel hybrid plasmonic nanostructures and devices for applications in optical communications and sensing.
the development of hybrid plasmonic waveguides and their applications in optical communication, optical sensing and optical force manipulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid plasmon polariton (HPP) is the most efficient optical energy confiner in the near field regime.

optical forces can be greatly enhanced in hybrid plasmonics, and the enhancement factor is strongly dependent on the dielectric constant of the substrate, the thickness and the width of the waveguide.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hybrid plasmonics is a promising candidate for the realization of integrated optical devices with subwavelength optical confinement, and thus can potentially lead to significant enhancement in the optical force.
hybrid plasmonic waveguides can enhance optical forces by more than one order of magnitude, and can achieve the same force with much smaller power consumption, as compared to dielectric waveguides.
the hybrid plasmonics can provide a new paradigm for nanophotonics.
